data.title: Modine stock surges on report naming Google as $4B data center customer
data.description:
Modine Manufacturing (MOD) shares surged 8% on Friday after Hunterbrook said that Google is the unnamed hyperscaler behind the company’s more than $4B long-term capacity agreement announced in May.

Modine had said on May 26 that it signed the agreement through 2029 with an unnamed strategic data center customer for its Airedale by Modine cooling solutions.

Hunterbrook said it found what appeared to be Modine’s internal data center database in a publicly accessible GitHub repository and that the files identified Google as the customer behind the agreement. The report said the database also showed another $4.5B of Google-related cooling demand, with about $433M booked.Modine makes cooling and thermal management equipment used in data centers and other industrial applications.

There is also about $3B of firm or likely commitments from Amazon Web Services, Crusoe, and other data center customers, bringing modeled demand in the database to nearly $23B. AWS accounted for more than half of the total, Hunterbrook said.

data.title: BLS benchmark revision could erase 200K reported jobs, Pantheon Macro warns
data.description:
The Bureau of Labor Statistics will release its preliminary estimate of the 2026 benchmark revision to payrolls next week and economists Samuel Tombs and Oliver Allen at Pantheon Macroeconomics are warning the numbers will reveal significant overstatement in reported job gains.

The firm projects that net job creation was around 200K lower in the 12 months through March 2026 than the establishment survey indicated—a discrepancy attributed almost entirely to structural data collection problems. The benchmark revision compares monthly establishment survey figures against the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages, which draws on comprehensive unemployment insurance tax records and is considered the gold standard of employment data.

Recent revisions have been sharply negative; last year's preliminary estimate showed payrolls 911K lower than reported for March 2025, eventually revised to -862K. The primary culprit is nonresponse bias: only about 30% of businesses contacted by the BLS now agree to participate in the establishment survey, down from a stable 60%-70% range throughout the 2010s. Businesses refusing to participate tend to be financially weaker than those willing to supply information, creating systematic distortion. 

Two other historical contributors—the birth-death model and counting of unauthorized workers—appear less problematic this cycle, the economists wrote.

The revision carries relevance for Federal Reserve policy deliberations, though the data release appears set to coincide exactly with Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, preventing the numbers from influencing his prepared remarks. Pantheon maintains its forecast that the fed funds mid-point will hold at 3.625% through December 2026.

data.title: Splash Beverage to rename as Endovia Health Sciences; shares up
data.description:
• Splash Beverage (SBEV) will change its corporate name to Endovia Health Sciences and begin trading on NYSE American under ticker EDVA at market open on August 24, 2026.
  • The rebranding marks the Company’s strategic shift from legacy beverage operations toward a diversified cannabinoid-based health sciences platform.
  • Endovia’s strategy focuses on commercial pharmaceutical assets, FDA-regulated human and veterinary therapeutics, and consumer wellness and beverage products.
  • Endovia is advancing CannEpil® through regulated human and veterinary development pathways in the U.S.
  • SBEV shares up 6.6%.

data.title: Nvidia makes minority investment in data center power facilitator Cloverleaf Infrastructure
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) entered into a strategic partnership with data center power facilitator Cloverleaf Infrastructure on Friday, which includes a minority investment from the chip giant.

Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but The Wall Street Journal, which first reported the news, said the chip giant could potentially invest hundreds of millions of dollars into Cloverleaf.

“AI is accelerating demand for digital infrastructure at an unprecedented scale and driving strong economic development opportunities for American communities,” said David Berry, Co-Founder and CEO of Cloverleaf, in a statement. “This partnership strengthens Cloverleaf's ability to identify and develop high-quality sites that provide the compute power for our country's growth and security. Together, we will help America's businesses and workers gain a critical edge.”

“AI factories are the infrastructure of the intelligence age, and land, power and shell are their foundation,” said Nvidia executive Nico Caprez. “Cloverleaf brings deep expertise in power and site development to create exceptional, long-lived sites for generations of accelerated computing. Together, we are accelerating the build out of AI infrastructure that will strengthen America's energy infrastructure and power the next wave of innovation.”

Cloverleaf handles signing power agreements with utility companies, which then allows developers to build on land and have access to power. The company has a pipeline of more than 10 GW of power, The Journal added. 

The deal is Nvidia's second energy-focused investment of the week. The Jensen Huang-led firm invested $1.5B into SB Energy, helping facilitate a data center deal in Ohio.

(This story has been updated to confirm the investment.)

data.title: Iranian president Pezeshkian signals push to bring war to an end
data.description:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian had reportedly called for an end to the U.S.-Iran conflict. 

“It would be better to end the war today, when we have power and dignity, and with the whole world acknowledging our victory,” Masoud Pezeshkian said, Bloomberg reported, citing the semi-official Iranian Students’ News Agency.

The comments come a day after U.S. President Donald Trump declared 'Economic D-Day' on Iran.

"ANY country that allows its financial institutions, businesses, airports, or government entities to provide any type of lifeline to Iran will itself face TREMENDOUS Economic Consequences," Trump had written on Truth Social. "Oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, front companies — It all needs to stop NOW."

Oil prices were slightly higher at the time of writing, with Brent futures (CO1:COM) up 0.52%, and crude oil futures rose 0.1% at the time of writing.

"The so-called "Economic D-Day" is a diversion from America's own crisis: unprecedented debt & surging interest costs," Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi had said on X.

On Monday, Trump had said that there were no talks that were ongoing or scheduled with Iran.

Pezeshkian's comments could be considered a pushback against some other Iranian officials, who believe that Tehran should continue to fight, Bloomberg said.

data.title: Refiner stocks are turning into one of this year's biggest winners
data.description:
U.S. refiners are on a roll this year, with several stocks more than doubling in value, as war-driven supply disruptions boost refining margins.

Shares of U.S. refiners have soared YTD (as of Thursday's close): PBF Energy  (PBF) +156.5%, Marathon Petroleum (MPC) +120.3%, Delek US (DK) +115.9%, Valero Energy (VLO) +109.8%, Par Pacific (PARR) +106.2%, HF Sinclair (DINO) +101.2%, Phillips 66 (PSX) +86%. 

The U.S. diesel crack — which measures the price difference between WTI futures and U.S. diesel futures, an indicator of refinery profitability — reached a record $102.20/bbl on Monday.

"Diesel cracks more than doubled since the start of the U.S.-Iran conflict," ING Economic and Financial Analysis noted this week. "Export restrictions from Russia, following repeated Ukrainian drone attacks on refineries, have reduced diesel availability, while disruptions affecting energy infrastructure elsewhere have added to concerns over supply and helped support prices."

Adding to the strain is China's move to restrict its fuel exports to avoid domestic shortages. The American refining industry is already operating near maximum processing capacity, with no ability to increase output.

"U.S. refiners have responded aggressively," said Ole Hansen, head of commodity strategy, Saxo. "Strong margins have encouraged high utilization and U.S. diesel exports have surged as buyers in Europe, Latin America and elsewhere compete for supply."

"But even this response has struggled to rebuild inventories. U.S. distillate stocks have fallen to exceptionally low seasonal levels despite strong refinery economics," Hansen pointed out.

The surge in diesel cracks is expected to impact farmers, who need fuel to power equipment needed for the ongoing harvest season.

"The result is a market that is about to enter its strongest seasonal demand period with very little margin for error, particularly because global gasoline also remains exceptionally tight," Bank of America strategists said.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices have cost U.S. consumers around $40B since the Iran war broke out, according to Brown University’s Climate Solutions Lab. 

"Higher diesel prices mean higher inflation across the economy," Investing Group Leader Bret Jensen warned earlier this month. "Almost every product that moves to market does so via rail, ship, or truck. All of these industries run on diesel fuel."

The Energy Information Administration expects high crack spreads through the end of 2026, which will support refinery margins.

But if the U.S. and Iran reach an agreement to end the war, Jensen expects a big selloff across refiners. "A very big if right now," he concluded.

data.title: Synergy CHC gets Nasdaq compliance notice over delayed Q2 filing; stock crashes
data.description:
• Synergy CHC (SNYR) announced on Friday that it received a Nasdaq notice over its delayed Q2 2026 Form 10-Q filing.
  • Nasdaq said the delay puts the company out of compliance with the listing rule, which requires timely filing of periodic reports with the SEC.
  • The notice has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of Synergy CHC common stock.
  • The company has until October 19, 2026, to submit a compliance plan to Nasdaq.
  • Nasdaq may give the company until February 10, 2027, to regain compliance.
  • Following the announcement, the stock crashed nearly 10% to ~$0.11 in the pre-market hours.

data.title: RenovoRx regains Nasdaq compliance
data.description:
RenovoRx (RNXT) announced on Friday that it has received a Nasdaq notification, confirming that the company has regained compliance with the minimum bid price requirement for continued listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market.

The Nasdaq Listing Qualifications Staff notified RenovoRx that the closing bid price of its common stock was at $1.00 per share or greater for the 10 consecutive business days from August 6, 2026, through August 19, 2026. Accordingly, RenovoRx has regained compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2), and Nasdaq has confirmed that the matter is now closed. 

The notification has no effect on the trading of the company’s common stock, which continues to trade on Nasdaq under the symbol “RNXT.”

Source: press release
